liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Dancin' in the Streets** (4 reviews): Runs about 25 minutes, with a jam featuring Jerry and Billy that follows; The Dancin' and the Jerry jam after it are called devastating, with fast rolling runs of notes [9][11][14][16]
- **Goin' Down the Road Feelin' Bad** (2 reviews): Weir tries out slide guitar on this song, which the reviewer regrets; Jerry's playing makes this song sound different and energized [7][17]
- **Candyman** (1 review): Jerry's voice sounded frail and quivering, fueling rumors of vocal problems [12]
- **Not Fade Away** (1 review): A hot fifteen-minute version comes after the drums [9]

## The recordings

- **gd79-01-12.claridge.kempka.309.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 17 songs; 145 min; rated 3.89/5 by 27 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the recording sound weak and the energy flat; Reviewer says the sound quality is poor; Reviewer considers it a nice audience tape that captures the feel of a 1979 show [10][11][15]
- **gd1979-01-12.167729.ShureSM57.Sublette.Noel.Goldey.t-flac2496**: source not stated; 16 songs; 156 min [3]
- **gd1979-01-12.163410.aud.Spectrum.howie.fulton.flac1644**: audience recording; 8 songs; 82 min [4]
- **gd1979-01-12.132217.aud.wise-claridge.fob.sony.ecm-280.flac16**: audience recording; 16 songs; 149 min; rated 4.5/5 by 4 [2]

## Around the show

- Reviewer says this was their very first concert [8]
- Noted as the last tour for Keith and Donna [10]
- Reviewer says America opened the Friday night show [12]
- Reviewer attended the makeup show on 1/5/79, using tickets from November 78 [12]
- Keith and Donna would soon leave the band, making the show bittersweet [16]
- Reviewer notes this was the only Goin' Down the Road Feelin' Bad played during 1979 [7]
- Show gets overlooked because the strong Nassau show came just before it [9]
- Show falls before Brent joins the band [15]
- Differs from the reviewer's expectations of 1979, despite some synthesizer sounds; Jerry's tone is grittier with more sustain [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-01-12.claridge.kempka.309.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Eddie Claridge; transferred by Jim Wise; source: Audience Recording: Sony ECM-280's [1]. Also: Taped from the balcony with Sony ECM-280 mics into a Sony TC158 deck, split at 30 feet; Discs came from Robert Donnelly; Jeff Kempka extracted them with cdparanoia on 5/3/2000 [1]
- **gd1979-01-12.167729.ShureSM57.Sublette.Noel.Goldey.t-flac2496**: taped by Kathy Sublette; transferred by DSF Transfer by Mark Goldey Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel May 02, 2024; source: Shure SM57 mics > Sony-TC158 (Dolby ??) > Master Cassettes [3]
- **gd1979-01-12.163410.aud.Spectrum.howie.fulton.flac1644**: taped by Howie form Long Island; transferred by Mark D Fulton; source: FOB Aud -> CM -> C -> C [4]. Also: Taped by Howie from Long Island; the transferor only received the second set, via a college friend; Samson and Delilah was not copied, and the drums were edited to fit on a CD; For this upload the drums were patched in from the Claridge/Wise recording [4]
- **gd1979-01-12.132217.aud.wise-claridge.fob.sony.ecm-280.flac16**: taped by Jim Wise and Eddie Claridge; transferred by Jim Wise; source: flac16/48kHz ; Cassette Audience Master Recorded 12'th Row FOB Dead Center by Eddie Claridge & Jim Wise; Sony ECM 280 Cardioid Condenser Microphones-Stand… [2]
